findings.summary: The earlier missing resolveConfig branch is now recovered: resolved.cache !== false gates normalization to {dir:viteConfig.cacheDir}; false survives. Combined with the original parser and ResultsCache passages, boolean cache:false suppresses that results.json route. This says nothing about independent Vite config, fork transform, debug, snapshot or reporter writes.

Fork createChildProcessChannel unconditionally passes cacheFs:true. RPC fetch creates project.tmpDir/<transformMode>, hashes module ids, and writes transformed code via write-then-rename with a direct-write fallback. These writes are separate from result-cache normalization. Project tmpDir/clearTmpDir behavior is in the preserved original passages; cleanup swallows errors, so debt needs observation.

Current vitest.config.ts uses bare __dirname in an ESM package. Bundle injects that binding and is the established unchanged-config route. Vite's runner supplies filename/dirname only on the import.meta object; its AsyncFunction parameter list contains only SSR helper bindings and has no bare __dirname. Native directly imports without injected binding. Neither alternate establishes compatibility for the unchanged config, and no alternate/config rewrite is selected.

Bundle uses esbuild build(write:false), then Vite itself mkdir/writes a timestamped .mjs under nearest node_modules/.vite-temp. It unlinks with an unawaited callback that ignores error; the directory remains. No node_modules or EACCES fallback writes adjacent to original config. cache:false, cacheDir and TMPDIR do not redirect this branch. Any later owned transient exception must preserve existing occupants, disallow unrelated deletion, and include actual cleanup verification.

Installed CLI supports finite run/watch control, boolean cache false, fork isolation, min/max workers, fileParallelism and singleFork. createForksPool uses child_process runtime, worker.js, workers/forks.js, teardown named export, and concurrentTasksPerWorker:1. singleFork or disabled fileParallelism bounds min/max to one; isolation remains true unless separately overridden. These are supported options, not an assembled or admitted argv. Preserve all 80 old and five prospective cases; no name filtering, manufactured skips, retries-as-success or missing-case acceptance.

Tinypool 2.2.0 WorkerInfo.destroy awaits the teardown task before starting its termination timeout and calling worker.terminate. ProcessWorker.terminate sends the default termination signal, schedules SIGKILL after 1000ms, and waits for that direct child exit. Therefore an unresolved teardown can prevent the internal termination phase from starting, and direct-child exit does not prove descendants gone. Vitest cleanup and esbuild stop similarly do not prove group quiescence. A separately admitted external captured-group deadline/cleanup/postflight remains essential.

createPool filters process.execArgv to profiler/diagnostic options plus module conditions but spreads process.env and config.env into workers. Those inherited values can override the earlier VITEST/TEST flags. VITEST_MIN_FORKS/MAX_FORKS affect normalization; UPDATE_SNAPSHOT can make snapshot mode all despite update:false; non-CI default snapshot mode is new. Empty reporter selection adds github-actions when GITHUB_ACTIONS=true. VITE_NODE_DEBUG_DUMP enables dump-file writes and may recursively remove the dump directory. A concrete future contract must bind these inputs and output ownership; no inherited-environment safety is assumed here.

The Vitest optimizer config hook treats absent enabled as false and translates the Vite6 disabled route into noDiscovery:true/include:[]; current project config has no optimizer enablement. Later normalized/serialized Vitest deps.optimizer fields default enabled:true, so a blanket claim that every optimizer field defaults false would be incorrect. Actual Vite optimizer setup is the controlling boundary. Coverage enabled:false, API:false and UI:false are explicit defaults; separate snapshot, attachment, reporter, browser, typecheck, debugger and profiling routes must not be inferred absent merely from result cache:false.

Installed Vitest happy-dom setup imports GlobalWindow/Window; teardownWindow awaits win.happyDOM.abort and calls win.close when present, otherwise cancelAsync. runBaseTests awaits environment teardown in finally. The actual happy-dom 21.0.4 Window/abort/close implementation is not in these 133 bodies, so these callers do not prove bounded cancellation, subprocess/network absence or final handle cleanup.

Recovered installed esbuild package.json/lib/main.js identify 0.28.1. Parent continuity states Vite's installed override edge resolves this version; that edge was not independently re-censused here. The JS honors a valid ESBUILD_BINARY_PATH, otherwise resolves the platform package/bin then a downloaded fallback; a zip/PnP branch can copy/chmod into node_modules/.cache/esbuild. Async service spawns the chosen command with --service=0.28.1 --ping, pipes stdin/stdout and inherits stderr; stop kills without awaiting child exit. Transform inputs over 1 MiB can use randomized os.tmpdir files. Exact selected native executable identity and platform/link/override conditions remain unclosed; no binary was run.

Unchanged setup scans immediate os.tmpdir agent-teams-vitest-home-* directories older than its cutoff, creates a home, and stubs worker HOME/USERPROFILE before each test; CODEX_HOME is not changed. An exclusive empty owned phase TMPDIR can contain that scan/home and fork/esbuild temporary files, while supervisor HOME/CODEX_HOME remain as-is. Setup cleanup is best effort, with its once flag set before removal. Direct installed Vitest avoids root test/test:ci scripts that build MCP+Host, but installed bundle work is still compiler work.
